key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=3% more than placebo) with OPSUMIT 10 mg vs placebo: nasopharyngitis/pharyngitis (20% vs 13%), headache (14% vs 9%), anemia (13% vs 3%), bronchitis (12% vs 6%), urinary tract infection (9% vs 6%), influenza (6% vs 2%). Key labeled risks include embryo-fetal toxicity, hepatotoxicity, and hemoglobin decrease (mean ~1.0 g/dL).

Summary information should include the total number of cases, a summary of key facts in those cases, with pertinent expert analysis of clinically relevant information from the case series. summary.text: OPSUMIT (macitentan) was approved via a standard-review NDA based on the single pivotal SERAPHIN morbidity/mortality trial; approval was subject to a REMS for teratogenicity risk and postmarketing requirements for hepatic risk surveillance. No accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, or priority-review designation was indicated.

citations.quote: The indication for this NDA is supported by a single, large, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study (AC-055-302/SERAPHIN) designed to evaluate the effect of macitentan compared to placebo on morbidity and mortality in patients with symptomatic PAH.
In accordance with section 505-1 of FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Opsumit (macitentan) to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the risk of teratogenicity.

We have determined that an analysis of spontaneous postmarketing adverse events reported under subsection 505(k)(1) of the FDCA will not be sufficient to assess a signal of a serious risk of hepatotoxicity for Opsumit (macitentan).

description.text: Updated Pediatric Use labeling based on pediatric PAH study (TOMORROW) in children with pulmonary arterial hypertension

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for changes to labeling (Section 8.4, Pediatric Use) based on the results of Protocol #AC-055-312, titled "A multicenter, open-label, randomized study with single-arm extension period to assess the pharmacokinetics, safety, and efficacy of macitentan versus standard of care in children with pulmonary arterial hypertension" (TOMORROW). This sNDA was submitted in response to a pediatric Written Request under the Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA).
